feed.title: Bausch / Jordan lab - Applied Neuroscience and Neurotechnologies
feed.subtitle: The Bausch / Jordan lab specializes in applied neuroscience and neurotechnology, pioneering in the exploration of fundamental brain functions such as memory and sleep in both epileptic patients and healthy individuals. Leveraging a multidimensional approach that includes intracranial recordings, surface EEGs, and custom-designed multimodal wearables, we aim to uncover novel insights into how internal states and external contexts affect epilepsy and memory.

entry.title: Nature publication
entry.content:
Excited to share that our new paper is out in Nature! https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09910-2

Rodent neurons often mix content & context. But humans? We found neurons encode content & context largely separately, then dynamically combine them. Rather than storing rigid combinations, context is dynamically reinstated. We saw co-activation of distinct content & context neurons. The strength of this signal predicts memory performance. With learning, coordinated firing emerges consistent with synaptic plasticity and pattern completion.

This suggests the brain supports flexible memory by reusing content representations while reconstructing context as needed. Huge thanks to all co-authors and feel free to apply, we are looking for excellent PhD candidates and PostDocs!
